title: Tailoring Education with GenAI: A New Horizon in Lesson Planning
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can support educators in creating customized lesson plans more efficiently and with better adaptation to learner needs. The authors focus on a “Learning Scenario Assistant” built around interactive prompt engineering, designed to behave like a teaching assistant, instructional designer, and subject expert. The central question is how a GenAI system can be structured to elicit detailed user requirements, generate a first draft lesson plan, and then support iterative revision and final human editing.

The intervention is an interactive mega-prompt workflow with several stages: a positioning prompt to orient the model, an interactive prompt that asks the user about audience, topic, goals, format, duration, examples, and optional extra questions, followed by iterative feedback cycles and a final human-led refinement step. The paper reports a case study using the tool to build a Digital Humanities course plan, with the authors progressively refining the plan based on user input. The evaluation also compares multiple LLMs, including ChatGPT, Llama, and Google Bard, across English and Greek learning-scenario generation.

The study context is educational planning for preschool, secondary school, and university levels, with an explicit example involving university freshmen in Communication, Media, and Culture in Greece. The evaluation combines quantitative ratings, qualitative expert feedback, and linguistic analysis of generated text. The authors conclude that newer models such as ChatGPT 4 and Llama 2 70B generally produce more relevant, personalized, and coherent lesson-planning outputs, and that GenAI can reduce lesson-planning time while supporting personalization. At the same time, they stress the need for human oversight, ethical use, and further testing, including randomized trials, to establish effectiveness more rigorously.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a preliminary, non-randomized evaluation with descriptive quantitative ratings and qualitative feedback rather than a controlled comparison of teacher outcomes. It is peer-reviewed/preprint-style empirical work, but the design does not meet strong causal credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical benefits for teacher planning efficiency, but it reports no formal effect size and provides only preliminary, descriptive evidence. The impact appears promising yet unclear in magnitude for broader populations.

interventions.use_case: interactive GenAI lesson-planning assistant that asks teachers follow-up questions, drafts lesson plans, and supports iterative revision and final proofreading across educational levels and languages

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that educators found the GenAI-generated lesson plans effective and significantly reducing lesson planning time. The evaluation across English and Greek scenarios indicates improved efficiency in generating customized lesson plans, but no formal effect size or statistical test is reported.
finding.measure: teacher-reported time savings; qualitative user satisfaction with lesson planning workflow; response time scores in Likert-based model comparison
